question: Would a RELISH evaluation measure our retrieval quality, or our corpus coverage?
note_on_original_host: The original RELISH host, relishdb.ict.griffith.edu.au, no longer resolves. This uses the ZB MED mirror of the FigShare record.
disclosures: A RELISH assessed article that is absent from our corpus cannot be retrieved by us at any rank, so it is an automatic loss unrelated to ranking. LitSense indexes ~38M PubMed abstracts, effectively all of PubMed, so this asymmetry favours them and must be stated wherever a comparison is drawn.

LitSense 2.0 reports on "the test portion" of RELISH. That split is not published with their paper, so our figures cannot be made byte-comparable to theirs; any comparison is indicative and has to say so.

RELISH is an article-to-article similarity task. Using it means querying with a seed article's abstract, which is the verbatim-text condition our own evaluation reports separately from composed questions, and it is the easier condition for every system.
verdict: Assessed-article coverage is only 33.6%, so a RELISH evaluation would largely measure the difference in corpus size rather than retrieval quality. Reporting it head-to-head against LitSense would be misleading in our own disfavour, and the honest use is a coverage-restricted analysis clearly labelled as such.
